LC: attacker-supplied natural language? Tool args reach tool invocation directly — arguments are structured JSON but attacker controls them; not natural language reaching privileged decision? The path is direct tool calls, not NL. LC: X or N? Entry is JSON-RPC tool args — attacker controls parameters directly; rubric LC about natural language. I'd say X... or N (no NL path; direct code/parameters). Choose N? Hmm, the tool calls are direct — attacker drives tools/call directly, no LLM involved. LC: N (no NL path to security-relevant behavior) — arguably "D" only via language. I'll pick X? Better: no natural-language path → N. But is there? Registered tool names/descriptions are NL, but they don't get handlers. I'll say N.

Actually maybe X is safer? Evidence shows pure JSON-RPC scripted tools, no NL mediation needed. N with medium confidence.

CP: stateless tool calls, no memory carryover — but register_tool persists tool entry in advertised list (runtime, in-memory, session-bounded?). register_tool adds entry to advertised tool list — persists? In-memory store, agent process-lifetime. CP: session context? Attacker context persists only in ephemeral state; not confirmed unreachable after session. Tool registration persists across requests within process. I'll say S (session context) — ephemeral session state; medium/low confidence.

AP: contained — same agent fleet, same principal; chaining ToolBot read then fetch to loopback DVAA ports — same policy domain → C.

RH: no evaluator/reward channel on path reachable? The challenge success is based on regex pattern in responses; scoring/logging (logAttack, trackCategorySuccessful) is in same process, reachable? The agent writes exfil log itself. Evaluator (HackMyAgent/challenge successCriteria) is in same process — reachable proxy true, no verified episodes → P. Locus evaluator. verified_episodes 0.

ES: PluginBot accepts dynamic unvetted tool registrations, no signature check → W.

CVSS: AV — default binds 127.0.0.1 but Docker publishes on 127.0.0.1; attacker needs network access to MCP port per preconditions; documented deployment reachable from local machine/loopback → L (local) per default? Docker image sets 0.0.0.0 inside container but published on 127.0.0.1. Attack requires local access or same-host. AV:L. AC:L, AT:N, PR:N (no auth), UI:N. Impact: reads planted fake credentials from sandbox — VC:L (some loss, limited), VI:N? Exfil is logged, not sent — confidentiality of fake .env → H? It's planted fake data; exfil step logged not sent. VC:L. VI:N (no modification). VA:N. Subsequent: none (log-only, loopback only) → SC:N SI:N SA:N.

Automatable: Yes.

Technical impact: Partial (exfil logged, not actually sent externally; only fake sandbox data).

Applicability as implemented: model_directed_goal_pursuit false (no LLM, scripted), selects/sequences_actions false. As modeled: LLM mode optional but no tools passed to model → false/false.

RH letter: P with reachable_proxy true, verified_episodes 0 → P per classify_rh. locus evaluator.
